definition: to provide room for; or to adjust to the needs or wishes of someone

examples.text: The new telescope dome can accommodate a mirror eight meters wide.
The treaty was rewritten to accommodate the smaller kingdom's fears.
We moved practice to Thursday to accommodate the players with Wednesday jobs.

confused.note: To accommodate is to make room for or adjust to; to accumulate is to pile up.

questions.passage: The original hall held only two hundred people. When membership tripled, the society built an extension to ______ the larger audience and added a ramp for members who could not manage the stairs.
questions.explanation: An extension makes room for more people.

distractors.why: Disregard means to ignore, the opposite of providing for the audience.
Censor means to suppress material, which does not fit.
Revoke means to cancel officially, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin modus, "measure": to fit to the measure

definition: to balance one effect with an opposite effect, so that there is no great change

examples.text: The cooling effect of the dust offset some of the warming.
Gains in the east were offset by losses in the west.
The money I saved by biking was offset by how much more I ate.

confused.note: To offset is to balance out; an onset is a beginning.

questions.passage: The bakery raised its prices in the spring. The increase was meant to ______ the rising cost of flour, which had nearly doubled since the previous harvest.
questions.explanation: Higher prices balance out higher costs.

distractors.why: Eradicate means to wipe out completely; raising prices balances the cost, it does not eliminate it.
Illuminate means to light up or clarify, which does not fit.
Chronicle means to record, which does not fit.

definition: continuing to do something despite difficulty; lasting for a long time

examples.text: A persistent cough can be a sign of something more serious.
Persistent rumors of gold drew settlers to the valley for decades.
My persistent little brother asked for a turn forty times in ten minutes.

confused.note: Persistent means not giving up or not going away; consistent means always behaving the same way.

questions.passage: The inventor was nothing if not ______. Her first ninety-nine designs for the lamp failed, some within seconds, yet she began the hundredth on the same afternoon that the ninety-ninth burned out.
questions.explanation: Starting again after ninety-nine failures shows she kept going despite difficulty.

distractors.why: Spontaneous means unplanned, which is not what her repeated effort shows.
Rhetorical relates to persuasive language, which does not fit.
Abrupt means sudden, which does not describe long, repeated effort.

definition: to make something known that was secret or hidden

examples.text: The archives, opened after fifty years, disclosed the terms of the secret treaty.
Authors must disclose who paid for their research.
The seller did not disclose that the bike had been in a crash.

confused.note: To disclose is to reveal; to enclose is to surround or put inside.

questions.passage: The law requires sellers to ______ any known defects. A homeowner who is aware that the roof leaks and says nothing can be made to pay for the repairs after the sale.
questions.explanation: Telling buyers about known defects is making hidden problems known.

distractors.why: Censor means to suppress information, the opposite of the legal duty.
Eradicate means to wipe out; the law requires telling, not fixing.
Converge means to come together, which does not fit.

definition: to make something less severe or extreme by adding something else

examples.text: The judge tempered the sentence with a promise of early release.
Ocean breezes temper the summer heat along the coast.
I tempered my criticism of the cake with praise for the frosting.

confused.note: To temper is to moderate; to tamper is to interfere with something.

questions.passage: The reviewer admired the novel but did not praise it without reservation. She ______ her enthusiasm with a warning that the final chapters were slow and the ending too neat.
questions.explanation: Adding a warning made her praise less extreme.

distractors.why: Jeopardized means put at risk, which does not fit.
Illuminated means lit up or clarified, which does not fit.
Revoked means cancelled entirely, but she still expressed enthusiasm.

definition: to say very strongly that something is wrong; or to sentence to a punishment

examples.text: The assembly condemned the invasion in a unanimous vote.
The village condemns the miller without hearing his side.
The coach condemned the cheap shot and benched her own player.

confused.note: To condemn is to declare wrong; to condone is to accept or overlook.

questions.passage: Leaders of both parties ______ the attack on the journalist. In a joint statement they called it "an assault on the freedom of every citizen" and demanded that those responsible be brought to trial.
questions.explanation: Calling the attack an assault and demanding trials is strong disapproval.

distractors.why: Condoned means accepted or excused, the opposite of their statement.
Chronicled means recorded, which does not capture their disapproval.
Disclosed means revealed, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin damnare, "to damage, to judge guilty"

definition: happening naturally, without being planned or forced

examples.text: The pile of oily rags burst into flame through spontaneous combustion.
Her spontaneous laugh breaks the silence of the funeral parlor.
We made a spontaneous decision to drive to the beach at midnight.

confused.note: Spontaneous means unplanned; simultaneous means happening at the same time.

questions.passage: No one had organized the celebration. It was entirely ______: as news of the victory spread, people simply walked out of their houses and began singing in the streets.
questions.explanation: A celebration no one organized happened naturally, without planning.

distractors.why: Rhetorical relates to persuasive speech, which does not fit.
Turbulent means wildly unsettled; the passage stresses that the celebration was unplanned.
Unanimous means agreed on by everyone, which is not the contrast with "organized."

partsNote: from Latin sponte, "of one's own accord"

definition: a written record of events in the order in which they happened

examples.text: The monk's chronicle is our only source for the kingdom's early years.
The novel takes the form of a chronicle kept by the town's schoolteacher.
My camera roll is an accidental chronicle of every meal I ate this year.

confused.note: A chronicle is a record of events; chronic means lasting a long time.

questions.passage: The diary is more than a private notebook. Kept daily for forty years by a ship's doctor, it is a detailed ______ of life in the port, noting every arrival, storm, and outbreak of fever.
questions.explanation: A daily record of events over forty years is a chronicle.

distractors.why: Jargon is specialized vocabulary, which does not fit.
A constituent is a component or a voter, which does not fit.
Longevity is long life, which does not fit.

definition: agreed on by everyone in a group

examples.text: The jury returned a unanimous verdict after an hour.
The panel was unanimous that the study should be repeated.
The vote for pizza was unanimous.

confused.note: Unanimous means everyone agrees; anonymous means unnamed.

questions.passage: The committee's nine members rarely agree on anything. On this question, however, the vote was ______: every one of them supported naming the new library after the teacher who had founded it.
questions.explanation: Every member voting the same way is complete agreement.

distractors.why: Turbulent means stormy, which does not describe a vote in which all agreed.
Abrupt means sudden, which is not the point.
Persistent means continuing, which does not fit.

definition: to mention something as an example or as support for what you are saying

examples.text: The paper cites more than two hundred earlier studies.
The judge cited a ruling from 1842 to justify her decision.
My sister cited "house rules" when she took the last cookie.

confused.note: To cite is to quote or refer to; a site is a place. Sight is vision.

questions.passage: In defending the plan to plant trees along the highway, the engineer ______ a study from Denmark, which found that roadside trees reduced accidents by slowing drivers down.
questions.explanation: Mentioning a study as support is citing it.

distractors.why: Revoked means cancelled, which does not fit.
Discredited means damaged the credibility of, but she used the study for support.
Eradicated means wiped out, which does not fit.

definition: to ignore something or treat it as unimportant

examples.text: The general disregarded the scouts' warning and marched into the valley.
The analysis disregards any reading taken during the storm.
I disregarded the "wet paint" sign and now have a green elbow.

confused.note: Use "regardless," not "irregardless," which is nonstandard.

questions.passage: The hikers chose to ______ the ranger's advice. Though she had told them the river was too high to cross, they waded in anyway and had to be pulled out by rope.
questions.explanation: Crossing despite the warning is ignoring the advice.

distractors.why: Cite means to mention as support, which is not what they did.
Accommodate means to adjust to, the opposite of ignoring advice.
Illuminate means to clarify, which does not fit.

definition: one of the parts that make up a whole; or a voter in a particular area

examples.text: Iron is a key constituent of the blood's oxygen-carrying protein.
The senator's constituents demanded that she oppose the tax.
Butter is the main constituent of my grandmother's cookies.

confused.note: A constituent is a part or a voter; a constitution is a set of basic laws or a person's physical makeup.

questions.passage: Chemists analyzing the ancient pigment found that its chief ______ was a mineral mined only in a single valley two thousand kilometers away, evidence of trade across a far greater distance than anyone had suspected.
questions.explanation: The main ingredient of the pigment is one of its component parts.

distractors.why: A chronicle is a record of events, which does not fit.
Posterity means future generations, which does not fit.
Jargon is specialized vocabulary, which does not fit.

definition: long life; the length of time something lasts

examples.text: The tortoise is famous for its longevity, often living past 150 years.
The dynasty's longevity owed much to its habit of marrying its rivals.
The longevity of my backpack, now in its sixth year, amazes my friends.

confused.note: Longevity is long life; longitude is a measure of east-west position.

questions.passage: The residents of the island are known for their ______. One in three lives past ninety, and researchers have spent decades studying their diet and habits for clues.
questions.explanation: Living past ninety in such numbers is long life.

distractors.why: Camaraderie is friendship within a group, which is not what the statistic shows.
Propriety is proper behavior, which does not fit.
Rigor is strictness or thoroughness, which does not fit.

definition: full of sudden changes, confusion, or violent movement

examples.text: The plane shook as it passed through turbulent air.
The turbulent decade saw four kings and two civil wars.
The first week of middle school was turbulent, but it settled down.

confused.note: Turbulent means violently unsettled; turbid means cloudy or muddy.

questions.passage: The years following the king's death were ______. Three rivals claimed the throne, the capital changed hands five times, and merchants who had traded peacefully for a generation fled abroad.
questions.explanation: Rival claims and a capital changing hands show confusion and violent change.

distractors.why: Arid means very dry, which does not fit.
Unanimous means in full agreement, the opposite of rivals fighting for the throne.
Ingenious means clever, which does not fit.

definition: sudden and unexpected; or brief and unfriendly in manner

examples.text: The fossil record shows an abrupt change in climate at this layer.
The chapter ends with an abrupt knock at the door.
The bus came to an abrupt stop, and my lunch slid off my lap.

confused.note: Abrupt means sudden or curt; corrupt means dishonest.

questions.passage: The symphony does not fade gently to a close. Its ending is ______: in the middle of a rising phrase the orchestra simply stops, leaving the audience unsure whether to applaud.
questions.explanation: Stopping in the middle of a phrase is sudden and unexpected.

distractors.why: Persistent means continuing, the opposite of stopping suddenly.
Spontaneous means unplanned, but the composer wrote the ending deliberately.
Rhetorical relates to persuasive language, which does not fit.

definition: relating to the art of persuasive speaking or writing; asked for effect, not for an answer

examples.text: The senator's rhetorical skill could turn a hostile crowd in ten minutes.
"What is in a name?" is a rhetorical question.
When my mom asks "Do you think money grows on trees?" the question is rhetorical.

confused.note: Rhetorical relates to persuasive language; theoretical relates to theory.

questions.passage: The lawyer's closing speech was a ______ triumph. She repeated a single phrase at the end of each paragraph, paused before every key point, and saved her most vivid image for the final sentence.
questions.explanation: Repetition, pauses, and a closing image are techniques of persuasive speaking.

distractors.why: Arid means dry or dull, the opposite of a vivid speech.
Turbulent means stormy, which does not fit.
Constituent refers to a component part, which does not fit.

definition: very dry, with little rain; or dull and lifeless

examples.text: Few crops can survive in the arid plains east of the mountains.
Nomads crossed the arid plateau only in winter, when the wells held water.
The textbook's arid prose put me to sleep by page three.

confused.note: Arid means very dry; acrid means sharp and bitter in smell or taste.

questions.passage: The region is among the most ______ on Earth. Some of its weather stations have never recorded a single drop of rain, and its soil is so dry that it has been used to test vehicles built for Mars.
questions.explanation: A place with no recorded rain is extremely dry.

distractors.why: Verdant means green with plant life, the opposite of this region.
Turbulent means stormy and unsettled, which does not fit.
Voluminous means very large or bulky, which does not fit.

definition: to remove parts of a book, film, or message because they are considered offensive or dangerous

examples.text: The wartime government censored every letter sent from the front.
The publisher censored two chapters, and the author never forgave him.
The school paper's adviser censored my joke about the cafeteria.

confused.note: To censor is to remove or block material; to censure is to criticize severely.

questions.passage: During the war, officials read every newspaper before it was printed. They ______ any article that mentioned troop movements, losses, or shortages, leaving blank white columns where the stories had been.
questions.explanation: Removing articles before printing is suppressing material.

distractors.why: Censured means criticized severely; the officials removed articles, they did not scold them.
Cited means quoted as support, which does not fit.
Propagated means spread widely, the opposite of removing articles.

definition: to make people stop believing in or respecting someone or something

examples.text: Rivals forged letters to discredit the minister.
Later experiments discredited the theory entirely.
One wrong answer on the quiz show discredited my claim to know everything about geography.

confused.note: To discredit is to damage credibility; discreet means careful and tactful.

questions.passage: The company hired investigators in an attempt to ______ its critic. They searched for anything in her past, an unpaid bill or an exaggerated résumé, that might make the public doubt her word.
questions.explanation: Making the public doubt her word is damaging her credibility.

distractors.why: Accommodate means to make room for or oblige, which does not fit.
Illuminate means to clarify, which was not the company's aim.
Ratify means to approve formally, which does not fit.

definition: very clever and original

examples.text: The device uses an ingenious system of mirrors to track the sun.
The ingenious lock had no key; it opened only to a pattern of knocks.
My sister's ingenious solution to the lost remote was to tape it to the couch.

confused.note: Ingenious means clever; ingenuous means innocent and trusting.

questions.passage: The engineers found an ______ way to cool the building without electricity. Hollow towers on the roof catch the wind and channel it over underground water tanks, sending chilled air through every floor.
questions.explanation: A clever, original cooling design is ingenious.

distractors.why: Ingenuous means naive and trusting; it only resembles the right word.
Abrupt means sudden, which does not fit.
Pedantic means fussy about small rules, which does not describe a clever design.

definition: to light something up; or to make something clearer and easier to understand

examples.text: A single lamp illuminated the cave painting for the first time in centuries.
The newly found letters illuminate the queen's reasons for abdicating.
The teacher's diagram illuminated a problem I had stared at for an hour.

confused.note: To illuminate is to light up or clarify; to eliminate is to remove.

questions.passage: Historians had long wondered why the expedition turned back within sight of its goal. A diary discovered in 2011 helps to ______ the mystery: its author describes a mutiny that the official report never mentioned.
questions.explanation: The diary makes the mystery clearer.

distractors.why: Censor means to suppress, the opposite of shedding light.
Jeopardize means to put at risk, which does not fit.
Offset means to balance out, which does not fit.

definition: to get rid of something bad completely

examples.text: A global vaccination campaign eradicated smallpox by 1980.
The new governor vowed to eradicate piracy along the coast.
We are trying to eradicate the ants in the kitchen without much success.

confused.note: To eradicate is to wipe out; to irradiate is to expose to radiation.

questions.passage: Health workers hope not merely to reduce the disease but to ______ it. If every child in the region can be vaccinated for three years running, the virus will have nowhere left to survive.
questions.explanation: Leaving the virus nowhere to survive is getting rid of it completely.

distractors.why: Propagate means to spread, the opposite of wiping out a disease.
Temper means to moderate; the sentence contrasts merely reducing with wiping out.
Chronicle means to record, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin radix, "root": to pull out by the root

definition: to officially cancel something so that it is no longer valid

examples.text: The king revoked the city's charter after the riots.
The agency revoked the lab's license to handle the virus.
My parents revoked my car privileges after the parking ticket.

confused.note: To revoke is to cancel; to evoke is to bring to mind.

questions.passage: The inspector found rats in the kitchen for the third time in a year. The city responded by ______ the restaurant's license, and it has not been permitted to reopen.
questions.explanation: Cancelling the license so the restaurant cannot operate is revoking it.

distractors.why: Ratifying means formally approving, the opposite of cancelling.
Citing means mentioning as support, which does not fit.
Disclosing means revealing, which does not fit.

definition: special words used by a particular group that are hard for others to understand

examples.text: The paper was so full of jargon that only specialists could follow it.
Sailors of the period spoke a jargon of English, Dutch, and Portuguese.
My brother's gaming jargon might as well be another language.

confused.note: Jargon is the technical vocabulary of a profession; argot is the slang of a closed group.

questions.passage: The doctor made a point of avoiding medical ______. She told patients that their "blood pressure was too high," never that they were "presenting with hypertension," and drew pictures when words failed.
questions.explanation: Technical terms that patients cannot understand are specialized vocabulary.

distractors.why: Camaraderie is friendship, which does not fit.
Propriety is proper behavior, which does not fit.
Longevity is long life, which does not fit.

definition: to come together from different directions and meet at one point

examples.text: The light rays converge at a point just behind the lens.
Three armies converged on the capital in the spring.
Every squirrel in the park converged on my dropped sandwich.

confused.note: To converge is to come together; to convert is to change.

questions.passage: Four highways ______ on the old market town. For centuries, travelers heading north, south, east, or west have had to pass through its central square.
questions.explanation: Highways from four directions meeting at one town come together.

distractors.why: Dissipate means to scatter and disappear, the opposite of meeting.
Plummet means to fall steeply, which does not fit.
Dwindle means to shrink gradually, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin vergere, "to bend, to incline": to incline together

definition: to put something in danger of being harmed or lost

examples.text: The general's delay jeopardized the entire campaign.
A single contaminated sample could jeopardize years of research.
Skipping practice the week before the final jeopardized my spot on the team.

confused.note: Jeopardize is the verb; jeopardy is the noun meaning danger.

questions.passage: The mayor warned that further delays would ______ the entire project. The federal grant that paid for the bridge would expire in December, and without it the city could not afford to finish the work.
questions.explanation: Delays that could cost the grant put the project in danger.

distractors.why: Ratify means to approve formally, which does not fit.
Propagate means to spread, which does not fit.
Peruse means to read carefully, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Old French jeu parti, "divided game": an even chance

definition: to spread an idea or belief widely; or to produce new plants or animals

examples.text: The pamphlets were printed to propagate the reformers' ideas.
Gardeners propagate the plant by cutting and rooting its stems.
My uncle uses the family group chat to propagate his opinions about baseball.

confused.note: To propagate is to spread or breed; to promulgate is to announce a law or idea officially.

questions.passage: The society was founded to ______ the new method of teaching reading. Its members printed guides, trained teachers in forty towns, and published a monthly journal describing their results.
questions.explanation: Printing guides and training teachers spreads the method widely.

distractors.why: Stifle means to hold back, the opposite of spreading.
Retract means to take back, which is not the society's aim.
Dissuade means to talk someone out of something, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin propago, "a shoot set to grow"

definition: great care and thoroughness; or strictness and severity

examples.text: The journal is known for the rigor of its review process.
Recruits were unprepared for the rigor of winter training.
My math teacher grades with a rigor that leaves no missing step unmarked.

confused.note: Rigor is strictness or thoroughness; vigor is energy and strength.

questions.passage: What distinguished her research was its ______. She repeated every measurement five times, recorded conditions in the laboratory hourly, and refused to publish until two other teams had confirmed her results.
questions.explanation: Repeating measurements and demanding confirmation show care and thoroughness.

distractors.why: Camaraderie is friendship in a group, which is not what the details show.
Propriety is socially proper behavior, which does not fit.
Posterity means future generations, which does not fit.

definition: to make someone feel that they do not belong or are no longer friendly toward you

examples.text: The king's taxes alienated the nobles who had once supported him.
His constant boasting alienates everyone at the table.
Correcting people's grammar at parties tends to alienate them.

confused.note: To alienate is to drive away; to alleviate is to ease.

questions.passage: The new coach's harsh methods quickly ______ the team's veterans. Several asked to be traded, and those who stayed stopped speaking to him except when the rules required it.
questions.explanation: Players who ask to leave and stop speaking to him have been driven away.

distractors.why: Dissuaded means talked out of something, which does not fit.
Ratified means formally approved, which does not fit.
Invalidated means made invalid, a word for claims and documents, not people.

definition: to take back a statement or offer; or to pull something back in

examples.text: Under pressure, the newspaper retracted its accusation.
A cat can retract its claws; a dog cannot.
I retracted my offer to share my fries when I saw how hungry my brother was.

confused.note: To retract is to take back; to detract is to take away from the value of something.

questions.passage: Six months after publication, the journal was forced to ______ the article. An investigation had shown that the photographs on which its conclusions rested had been altered.
questions.explanation: Withdrawing a published article is taking it back.

distractors.why: Propagate means to spread, the opposite of withdrawing an article.
Jeopardize means to endanger, which does not fit.
Peruse means to read carefully, which does not fit.

definition: to persuade someone not to do something

examples.text: Advisers tried to dissuade the king from invading in winter.
Nothing her mother says can dissuade the heroine from leaving.
I tried to dissuade my friend from cutting her own bangs.

confused.note: To persuade is to talk someone into something; to dissuade is to talk them out of it.

questions.passage: Friends and family all tried to ______ the young sailor from attempting the crossing alone. They pointed to the season, the age of her boat, and the three experienced crews that had been lost on the same route.
questions.explanation: Giving reasons not to go is trying to talk her out of it.

distractors.why: Alienate means to make hostile, and it does not fit "from attempting."
Stifle means to hold back a feeling or activity, which does not fit this construction.
Ratify means to approve formally, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin suadere, "to advise": to advise away

definition: to show that something is wrong or to make it no longer legally acceptable

examples.text: A single contaminated sample would invalidate the whole experiment.
The court invalidated the election after finding thousands of forged ballots.
A typo in the email address invalidated my contest entry.

confused.note: Invalidate is the verb; invalid, as an adjective, means not valid.

questions.passage: The discovery that half the survey's respondents had answered twice ______ its results. The researchers had no choice but to discard the data and begin again.
questions.explanation: Duplicate answers made the results worthless.

distractors.why: Ratified means formally approved, the opposite of throwing results out.
Propagated means spread, which does not fit.
Dwindled means shrank, and it cannot take an object.

definition: to stop something from happening or developing; to hold back

examples.text: Heavy taxes stifled trade in the port for a generation.
She stifles a laugh behind her fan.
I stifled a yawn during my uncle's slideshow.

confused.note: To stifle is to hold back or smother; to stiffen is to become rigid.

questions.passage: Critics argued that the school's strict rules ______ creativity. Students who were told exactly what to draw, and penalized for departing from the model, soon stopped trying anything new.
questions.explanation: Rules that stop students from trying new things hold creativity back.

distractors.why: Jeopardized means endangered; the passage says creativity was actually suppressed.
Perused means read carefully, which does not fit.
Propagated means spread, the opposite of holding back.

definition: a feeling of friendship and trust among people who spend time together

examples.text: The camaraderie of the trenches outlasted the war by fifty years.
The novel captures the camaraderie of a night shift in a small-town bakery.
The best part of the team is the camaraderie on the long bus rides.

confused.note: Camaraderie is the spirit of friendship in a group; a comrade is a companion.

questions.passage: Veterans of the expedition remember its hardships less than its ______. Forty years later they still gather each spring, and several say that they have never again felt so close to any group of people.
questions.explanation: Lasting closeness among people who shared an experience is friendship and trust.

distractors.why: Rigor is strictness or thoroughness, which is not what they treasure.
Posterity means future generations, which does not fit.
Propriety is proper behavior, which does not fit.

definition: all the people who will live in the future

examples.text: The explorer kept a careful journal for posterity.
The poet wrote for posterity, certain that her own age would never understand her.
My mom records every school concert for posterity, to our great embarrassment.

confused.note: Posterity means future generations; prosperity means wealth and success.

questions.passage: The architect knew that the cathedral would not be finished in his lifetime. He was content to build for ______, trusting that people not yet born would one day stand beneath the completed dome.
questions.explanation: Building for people not yet born is building for future generations.

distractors.why: Camaraderie is friendship among companions, which does not fit.
Prosperity means wealth; it resembles the right word but means something else.
Rigor is strictness, which does not fit.

definition: to gradually disappear or make something disappear; to waste

examples.text: The morning fog dissipated as the sun warmed the valley.
The heir dissipated the family fortune within a decade.
My nervousness dissipated once I started speaking.

confused.note: To dissipate is to fade away or waste; to disseminate is to spread widely.

questions.passage: The crowd's anger did not last. It ______ as soon as the mayor stepped onto the balcony and announced that the factory would stay open after all.
questions.explanation: Anger that fades away after good news disappears.

distractors.why: Converged means came together at a point, which does not describe anger fading.
Propagated means spread, the opposite of fading.
Plummeted means fell steeply, a word for prices and heights more than for a mood that fades away.

partsNote: from Latin supare, "to throw": to throw apart

definition: to give official approval to an agreement so that it becomes valid

examples.text: Nine states had to ratify the constitution before it took effect.
The treaty limiting emissions was ratified by sixty countries.
The student council ratified the new dress code by a single vote.

confused.note: To ratify is to approve formally; to rectify is to correct.

questions.passage: The two presidents signed the treaty in June, but it did not take effect at once. Each country's parliament first had to ______ it, a process that took nearly two years.
questions.explanation: Parliaments giving official approval to a treaty ratify it.

distractors.why: Retract means to take back, the opposite of approving.
Rectify means to correct; it resembles the right word but means something else.
Nullify means to cancel, which would keep the treaty from taking effect.

partsNote: from Latin ratus, "fixed, settled": to make fixed

definition: to make something lose its legal force or its effect

examples.text: The court nullified the law as contrary to the charter.
A leak in the chamber nullified the experiment's results.
One missed free throw nullified our comeback.

confused.note: To nullify is to cancel; to mollify is to soothe.

questions.passage: The agreement contained a clause that could ______ the entire contract. If either company was sold to a foreign buyer, every promise in the document would at once cease to have any force.
questions.explanation: A clause that ends all the contract's force cancels it.

distractors.why: Ratify means to approve and make valid, the opposite of cancelling.
Peruse means to read carefully, which does not fit.
Alienate means to make hostile, which does not fit a contract.

partsNote: from Latin nullus, "none": to make nothing

definition: to fall very quickly from a high level or position

examples.text: The falcon plummets toward its prey at over three hundred kilometers an hour.
The value of the currency plummeted when the bank closed.
The temperature plummeted twenty degrees overnight.

confused.note: To plummet is to fall fast; to plumb is to measure depth or explore thoroughly.

questions.passage: Sales of the magazine did not decline slowly. They ______: within six months of the scandal, circulation had fallen from two million copies to fewer than three hundred thousand.
questions.explanation: Falling from two million to under three hundred thousand in six months is a rapid drop.

distractors.why: Dwindled means shrank gradually, but the first sentence says the decline was not slow.
Converged means came together, which does not fit.
Dissipated means faded away; the figures describe a sudden steep fall.

definition: very large; containing a great deal; said of writing, very long and detailed

examples.text: The general's voluminous correspondence fills forty archive boxes.
The heroine hides the letter in the folds of her voluminous sleeves.
My backpack is voluminous enough to hold a week of forgotten lunches.

confused.note: Voluminous means very large or lengthy; luminous means glowing.

questions.passage: The scientist's notes were ______. Over a career of fifty years she filled more than three hundred notebooks, recording every observation, however small, in tiny, careful handwriting.
questions.explanation: Three hundred filled notebooks are a great quantity of writing.

distractors.why: Pedantic means fussy about small rules, which is not what the count of notebooks shows.
Verdant means green with vegetation, which does not fit.
Remiss means careless about duty, the opposite of such careful recording.

definition: behavior that is socially and morally correct

examples.text: The court's strict sense of propriety forbade anyone to sit before the queen.
The aunt is shocked less by the theft than by the lack of propriety.
My grandmother questions the propriety of wearing pajamas to the grocery store.

confused.note: Propriety is proper behavior; property is something owned.

questions.passage: Members of the board questioned the ______ of the gift. Even if no law forbade it, they said, a judge should not accept an expensive watch from a lawyer who regularly appeared in her courtroom.
questions.explanation: Whether accepting the gift is morally correct is a question of proper conduct.

distractors.why: Camaraderie is friendship, which is not what the board questioned.
Longevity is long life, which does not fit.
Rigor is strictness or thoroughness, which does not fit "of the gift."

definition: of the highest quality; excellent

examples.text: The city was famous for the superlative skill of its goldsmiths.
The critic called it a superlative performance, the best of the decade.
My aunt makes superlative dumplings that vanish in minutes.

confused.note: Superlative means of the highest quality; superfluous means more than needed.

questions.passage: Reviewers agreed that the orchestra's playing was ______. Several called the concert the finest they had heard in years, and one wrote that she could not imagine the symphony performed better.
questions.explanation: "The finest in years" describes playing of the highest quality.

distractors.why: Remiss means negligent, which does not fit praise.
Pedantic means overly concerned with small details, which is not praise.
Indomitable means impossible to defeat; the reviewers praise quality, not resilience.

definition: impossible to defeat or discourage

examples.text: The indomitable queen ruled from exile for twenty years and returned to her throne.
The heroine's indomitable spirit survives prison, shipwreck, and her relatives.
My grandmother has an indomitable will and a ninety-year-old's knees.

confused.note: Indomitable means unconquerable; indubitable means impossible to doubt.

questions.passage: Illness confined the painter to bed for the last ten years of her life. Her will was ______, however: she had a mirror fixed above her and went on working, with brushes tied to long sticks, until the week she died.
questions.explanation: Painting from her sickbed for ten years shows a will that could not be defeated.

distractors.why: Remiss means negligent, which does not fit.
Verdant means green and lush, which does not fit.
Voluminous means very large, which does not describe a will.

partsNote: from Latin domitare, "to tame": not able to be tamed

definition: to read something, especially in a careful or thorough way

examples.text: The king perused the treaty for an hour before signing.
The detective peruses the guest book and finds a familiar hand.
I perused the menu twice and still ordered the same sandwich as always.

confused.note: To peruse is to read carefully; to pursue is to chase or follow.

questions.passage: The lawyer did not sign the contract at once. She took it home to ______ over the weekend, reading each of its ninety clauses twice and making notes in the margin.
questions.explanation: Reading each clause twice with notes is careful reading.

distractors.why: Ratify means to approve formally, which she had not yet done.
Retract means to take back, which does not fit.
Nullify means to cancel, which does not fit.

definition: green with growing plants

examples.text: Satellite images show the verdant strip along the river cutting through the desert.
The travelers descend at last into a verdant valley.
After a wet spring, our usually brown lawn is verdant.

confused.note: Verdant means green and lush; verbose means wordy.

questions.passage: After three weeks of crossing bare rock and sand, the caravan reached the oasis. The travelers stared at its ______ palms and gardens as if they had forgotten that anything could be green.
questions.explanation: Palms and gardens that are green describe lush vegetation.

distractors.why: Arid means very dry, which describes the desert they had crossed.
Pedantic means fussy about rules, which does not fit.
Voluminous means very large or bulky, which is not the contrast with bare rock.

definition: too concerned with small details or rules, especially in showing off knowledge

examples.text: The pedantic tutor interrupts the love scene to correct a verb.
The clerk's pedantic insistence on the proper seal delayed the pardon by a day.
It is pedantic to point out that a tomato is technically a fruit.

confused.note: Pedantic means fussy about minor details; pedestrian means dull and ordinary.

questions.passage: The reviewer's objections struck most readers as ______. He devoted three paragraphs to a misplaced comma on page forty and said nothing about whether the book's argument was sound.
questions.explanation: Dwelling on a comma while ignoring the argument is fussing over small details.

distractors.why: Superlative means excellent, which does not describe petty objections.
Indomitable means unconquerable, which does not fit.
Verdant means green and lush, which does not fit.

definition: a person who falsely claims to have special knowledge or skill

examples.text: The charlatan sold bottled river water as a cure for every illness.
The village is taken in by a charlatan who claims to speak with the dead.
The "psychic" at the fair was an obvious charlatan who guessed my name wrong twice.

confused.note: A charlatan is a fraud; a chaplain is a member of the clergy.

questions.passage: The man who called himself a professor was exposed as a ______. He had never attended a university, the degrees on his wall were printed in his own basement, and his "miracle tonic" was colored sugar water.
questions.explanation: Faking degrees and selling sugar water as medicine is falsely claiming expertise.

distractors.why: An antecedent is something that came before, which does not fit.
A constituent is a component or voter, which does not fit.
A benefactor helps others, the opposite of someone who cheats them.

definition: careless about doing something that you should do

examples.text: The governor was remiss in failing to repair the levee before the rains.
The hostess feels remiss for not having introduced her guests.
I would be remiss if I did not thank my sister for driving me every morning.

confused.note: Remiss means negligent; amiss means wrong or out of place.

questions.passage: The safety board concluded that the airline had been ______. Mechanics had reported the worn cable three times, and on each occasion managers had postponed the repair.
questions.explanation: Postponing a reported repair three times is careless neglect of duty.

distractors.why: Superlative means excellent, the opposite of this conduct.
Indomitable means unconquerable, which does not fit.
Voluminous means very large, which does not fit.

definition: to become gradually smaller, fewer, or weaker

examples.text: The herd dwindled from thousands to a few dozen within a decade.
The army's supplies dwindled as winter closed the roads.
My enthusiasm for the group project dwindled with every meeting.

confused.note: To dwindle is to shrink gradually; to dawdle is to waste time.

questions.passage: The village once had three hundred residents. As young people left for the cities, its population ______ year by year, until only a dozen elderly farmers remained.
questions.explanation: Shrinking year by year to a dozen is a gradual decrease.

distractors.why: Plummeted means fell suddenly, but the decline here took many years.
Converged means came together, which does not fit.
Propagated means multiplied or spread, the opposite of shrinking.

definition: something that existed or happened before another thing and is related to it

examples.text: The uprising had its antecedents in a tax revolt thirty years earlier.
The paper traces the antecedents of the theory to work done in the 1920s.
The antecedent of "it" in my essay was unclear, so my teacher circled it.

confused.note: An antecedent is something that came before; a precedent is an earlier case used as a guide.

questions.passage: The modern novel did not appear from nowhere. Scholars have identified its ______ in the letters, diaries, and travel journals of the previous century, forms from which early novelists borrowed freely.
questions.explanation: Earlier forms that led to the novel came before it and are related to it.

distractors.why: Charlatans are frauds, which does not fit.
Constituents are component parts, not earlier forms.
Posterity means future generations, the opposite of what came before.
